subject: Traffic diversion notice & config-validation request — immediate action required
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Soteria Health <ops@soteriahealth.com>, Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@edgecorp.net>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 02 Dec 2028 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Traffic diversion notice & config-validation request — immediate action required

Hi Alicia / Soteria ops team,

Quick heads up — at ~14:40 UTC we observed elevated routing failures out of the primary US edge region and a correlated increase in failed handshakes for the EU peering fabric. Our mitigation is to divert affected tenants to the secondary routing plane (regional sidecars) while we validate the peering fabric.

What we need from you right now:
- Confirm that your edge connector is configured to accept the alternate endpoint: alt-ingress.redwood.ai:443 (TLS certs are the same).
- If you have IP allowlists, please add this CIDR block: 35.182.192.0/22 (temporary).
- Reply with the expected time window where you can accept a 1–2 minute connection reset for config application.

We attached a small patch (routing-config-patch.diff.txt) that some customers may apply to speed TTL reductions on their side; do not apply unless you can tolerate brief reconnects. We will also share a short validation checklist after you confirm.

Impact: a subset of requests from our US and EU region saw 502/504 for up to 6 minutes. APAC saw increased token latencies due to cross-region failover for some routed tenants. No token leaks or data exposure — logs attached for your review.

I will coordinate the switchover and remain on this thread for the next 3 hours. Please escalate to your network lead if you need phone support: +1 415 555 0104 (oncall).

— Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Account Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

Attachments: routing-config-patch.diff.txt, support-logs-UTC-2028-12-02.zip

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@edgecorp.net>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Soteria Health <ops@soteriahealth.com>
Date: Sat, 02 Dec 2028 15:34:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Traffic diversion notice & config-validation request — immediate action required

Thanks Mateo — we see increased 5xx errors on our side too and are already paged.

We can accept the alternate endpoint, but we need clarification:
- Will the diversion preserve session affinity for our long-running websocket sessions?
- We cannot add new CIDRs to our production allowlist without a change request; can you provide a secure hostname-only option (SNI)?

If there is a brief connection reset window we can schedule it between 17:00–17:15 PST (UTC+0: 01:00). If you can confirm preservation of session tokens and an SNI-only option, we'll proceed.

Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Sr. Platform Ops, Soteria Health
ops@soteriahealth.com

On Sat, Dec 2, 2028 at 15:12 Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Quick heads up — at ~14:40 UTC we observed elevated routing failures out of the primary US edge region and a correlated increase in failed handshakes for the EU peering fabric...

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 02 Dec 2028 15:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Traffic diversion notice & config-validation request — internal ops notes

Mateo / team — internal notes and steps (runbook excerpt):

1) Alternate access: we support SNI-only for the alternate endpoint. Use alt-ingress.redwood.ai with SNI "soteria.ops.redwood.ai"; no IP allowlist change required if you use SNI and TLS verification passes.
2) Session affinity: sidecar diversion will attempt to preserve affinity via KV-backed sticky cookies; long-lived websockets will likely re-establish under the alternate plane with a short reconnection. Token continuity is preserved — no token rotation required.
3) If they prefer to avoid any reconnection window, we can do an in-place route heal (takes longer and is best-effort).

Action for us:
- Mateo: provide a one-page validation checklist + expected window (you already proposed 17:00–17:15 PST).
- Olga: pre-warm their secondary routing plane and push the small TTL change to expedite failover.
- Marissa: confirm SLA implications and note the incident for the postmortem (INC-48392).

I attached the recent aggregated logs. I will stand by on Slack channel #inc-48392 for coordination.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Support Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: support-logs-UTC-2028-12-02.zip

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@edgecorp.net>, Soteria Health <ops@soteriahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 04 Dec 2028 09:22:00 -0600
Subject: Follow-up: diversion completed & post-incident next steps

Alicia — thank you for the quick response and for accepting the 17:00 PST window. Summary and next steps below.

What we did (summary):
- 17:02 PST: Enabled diversion to alt-ingress.redwood.ai using SNI-only for Soteria Health.
- 17:03–17:06 PST: Observed short reconnects on ~0.6% of websocket sessions; KV-backed affinity restored sessions within ~10s on average.
- 17:08 PST: Error rates returned to baseline across US and EU regions. APAC latency normalized by 17:20 PST after regional rebalancing.

Customer validation asked/received:
- SNI-only connectivity was successful (no IP allowlist changes needed).
- No token rotations were required; token continuity observed.

Artifacts and invites:
- Incident ticket: INC-48392 (HubSpot) — https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/##/ticket/INC-48392
- Consolidated logs and routing diff: attached.
- Postmortem working session: Wed 2028-12-06 10:00 PST — invite sent to your ops calendar. We will share the draft RCA beforehand.

Next actions for Redwood:
- Marissa: produce the customer-facing postmortem draft and include a timeline + mitigation recommendations.
- Olga: run a validation sweep on inter-region peering and propose a permanent routing preference to reduce single-plane exposure.
- Ben & I: follow up after the postmortem to propose a safe automated retry policy for websocket reconnections.

Alicia, if you'd like, we can keep the alternative endpoint on a soft failover for 72 hours and perform a controlled peering revalidation during low traffic. Please confirm if that’s acceptable.

Thanks again for your fast collaboration. Sorry for the interruption — we’ll be in touch with the detailed postmortem draft no later than Tue 2028-12-05 EOD PST.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai

Attachments: routing-config-patch.diff.txt, support-logs-UTC-2028-12-02.zip
